Create your own goal after looking around at the lets plays and stories you find.

It's easy to get overwhelmed when you feel like you should be doing everything. Instead set smaller goals for yourself, particularly with the newest add on where you can develop one province it might be a good idea to start as an HRE elector. This will give you the chance to do a bit of warring, have quite a few allies, play around with the Papal game, and reform eventually when/if you want to.

It doesn't focus on the economics, world diplomacy, colonization so much as carving out your little home in Europe, hopefully that will give you a solid understanding of the resources you can use when trying harder challenges.

(Like super Ulm! where you start and stay as a one province minor just building up that one little fellow until you're a beast.)

A good starting nation to play is Spain. It is isolated from most of the politics and warring of the other nations; if you keep France as a friend, then you won't need to get into a defensive war for a very, very long time. They have access to all of the gameplay systems, including colonization, war, alliances, etc., so it makes a good starting nation since you can try everything but are still isolated enough where ignoring certain aspects won't doom you. They are also big and rich enough to afford to defend themselves should it come to that.

It's also a great starting point to learn the most important aspect of the game: trade. Since Spain has a good deal of control over a trade node, it can become very, very rich if you learn the trade game, which every nation in the game needs to play. Every game becomes a game about controlling trade, so Spain is a very good starting nation to learning trade. Try having this goal: having majority control over Seville and all of Mediterranean trade.

If you have trade down pat, you'll be able to finance your ambitions when you go to master the other aspects, from warfare, colonization, religion, etc.

Spain is a good way to start, and this advice is key; "f you keep France as a friend, then you won't need to get into a defensive war for a very, very long time." Just keep up the Improve Relations w/ France and you should be in the clear.

It's a good way to learn colonization, learn how to siege and conquer (Granada), learn how to fight on the ocean and invade Northern Africa, learn how the Curia works as a Catholic nation, then watch how the Protestant Reformation spreads across northern Europe. A good early goal would be the achievement to get the historical Spanish colonies, as well as to complete the Iberian Wedding event and form Spain.
